additions.reason: Line 4 of the source text uses explicit bechina language: 'עַל־יְדֵי הַכְּתָב אֶפְשָׁר לְהַכִּיר הַנֶּפֶשׁ וּפְנִימִיּוּת הַנֶּפֶשׁ... בִּבְחִינַת: אָנֹכִי'. The Rebbe states that writing reveals the soul's inwardness 'in the bechina of אנכי'. The Zohar cited there (Shabbat 105a: אֲנָא נַפְשִׁי כְּתַבִית יְהַבִית) explains that when God said אנכי at Sinai, He gave His own soul into the text — meaning אנכי is the bechina of the innermost Shekhinah (שְׁכִינְתָּא פְּנִימִיּוּת). The Rebbe confirms this directly: 'אָנֹכִי – דָּא שְׁכִינְתָּא פְּנִימִיּוּת'. Thus אנכי is an aspect of פנימיות הנפש (since the Shekhinah is a bechina of the soul, as stated in line 5: 'הַשְּׁכִינָה הִיא בְּחִינַת נֶפֶשׁ'). This belongs in Package 1 as a bechina-equivalent of פנימיות הנפש and שכינתא פנימיות.

additions.reason: Line 4 of the source text presents a direct Zoharic bechina statement: 'אֲנִי – נוֹטְרִיקוֹן: אֲנָא נַפְשִׁי יְהַבִית – דָּא שְׁכִינְתָּא חִיצוֹנִיּוּת'. The word אני (the abbreviated form) is identified as a bechina of שכינתא חיצוניות (the external/outer dimension of the Shekhinah), while אנכי (the full form) is identified as שכינתא פנימיות. This creates a bechina pair within the teaching: the outer Shekhinah vs. the inner Shekhinah. Both are in the domain of the soul/Shekhinah (good polarity), but they represent different dimensions — outer and inner. שכינתא חיצוניות is the lesser bechina (outer soul, the action of writing), while שכינתא פנימיות is the higher bechina (inner soul, the inwardness revealed). Both belong in Package 1 as aspects of the soul-domain. The teaching uses this outer/inner distinction to explain why speech is greater than writing: speech reveals the soul itself, while writing reveals only the outer action of the soul.

additions.reason: Line 6 of the source text uses direct bechina language: 'עַל־יְדֵי הַכְּתָב, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת כ''. Writing (כתב) is explicitly declared to be a bechina of the כ' letter (אות כ"ף), which is already in Package 1 as a bechina of כתר (edge 1529). The three-step chain runs: כתב = אות כ"ף = כתר = פנימיות הנפש — all bechina relationships stated within this Torah. The act of writing is therefore an aspect of the same innermost-soul domain. Note: כתב is the instrument through which the tzaddik perceives the writer's soul — it is not a cause of soul-revelation in the eitza sense; it is, in this Torah, a bechina-equivalent (same essential nature) of the innermost dimension of the person, because the letter כ' that comprises כתב IS a bechina of כתר/פנימיות הנפש. The teaching's logic is identity, not causation.

concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: Line 2 mentions 'עוֹלַם אֱמוּנָה' as the source-world from which faith is drawn. However, it is described as a conceptual explanation ('דְּהַיְנוּ שֶׁיֵּשׁ עוֹלָם אֱמוּנָה') rather than a bechina statement. The Rebbe does not say 'שרש האמונה הוא בחינת עולם האמונה' — he is explaining what 'root of faith' means. The explicit bechina formulation applies to שרש האמונה = פנימיות האמונה (edge 2503), not to עולם האמונה as a separate node. Excluded per framework strictness: explanatory/definitional language is not the same as a bechina declaration.

Lines 7-8 discuss that speech (דיבור) with the true tzaddik is greater than writing, and quote Song of Songs 5:6 ('נַפְשִׁי יָצְאָה בְדַבְּרוֹ') to argue that 'הַדִּבּוּר הוּא הַנֶּפֶשׁ בְּעַצְמוֹ'. While this is a strong identification, the Rebbe's language here is argumentative comparison ('הוּא הַנֶּפֶשׁ בְּעַצְמוֹ' in context of explaining WHY speech is higher) rather than a formal bechina declaration (no 'בְּחִינַת' marker). The verse citation supports the argument rather than establishing דיבור as a bechina node. This is borderline; conservative reading excludes it. If included, it would belong in Package 1 as an aspect of the soul/inner-dimension cluster.

Line 7 describes writing as 'פְּעֻלַּת הַנֶּפֶשׁ' (action/expression of the soul) to explain why speech is higher — speech is the soul itself while writing is only the soul's action. This is a descriptive characterization, not a bechina declaration. The Rebbe uses it in an explanatory/comparative context ('הַכְּתָב אֵינוֹ רַק פְּעֻלַּת הַנֶּפֶשׁ'), and no bechina-marker (בְּחִינַת) is used. Excluded.

The true tzaddik appears repeatedly (lines 1, 7, 8) as the agent who perceives the soul through writing or speech. He is not given a bechina-label in this Torah — he is the subject/perceiver of the teaching, not an aspect being equated to another concept. No bechina declaration. Excluded.
